features.description: Every origin command of a merge runs through `origin_try` in lib/record.sh with bounded backoff (`ORIGIN_WAITS`), a GitHub refusal is never retried, and the outage stubs (tests/stub-git-down.sh, `STUB_GH_DOWN`) copy the real git and gh lines.
steps: tests/fixtures/git-push-rejected.txt holds the incident's two stderr lines with placeholders, ` ! [remote rejected] <ref> -> <ref> (failure)` then `error: failed to push some refs to '<url>'`; tests/fixtures/gh-down.txt is the stderr of a real gh pointed at a refusing local port (`GH_HOST=localhost:1 GH_REPO=localhost:1/o/r gh pr view 1`, run in the scratch directory /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-11-04-2, which is no git repo), saved as printed and never typed from memory.

tests/stub-git-down.sh is a `git` wrapper put first on PATH for a run (as tests/checks/15-run-4-same-but-queue-parked-debrief-tmux.sh's gcfail/git is): while `$STUB_DIR/origin-down` exists (a count, or `until <epoch>`), `fetch`, `push` and `ls-remote` whose remote is origin fail: push prints the fixture with the ref and url substituted on stderr, fetch prints nothing and exits 128; a count is decremented per failure and the file removed at 0; every other call execs the real git. Checks in a new tests/checks/88-origin-outage.sh (`# tier: slow` on line 2), written first and watched failing: with a count of 2 the first two pushes print the ` ! [remote rejected]` line and the third reaches origin.git.

tests/stub-gh.sh: `STUB_GH_DOWN=<n>` makes `pr view`, `pr create` and `pr merge` fail the first n calls with gh-down.txt's line on stderr; `STUB_REFUSE_MERGE`'s stderr becomes the real `GraphQL: Head branch was modified. Review and try the merge again. (mergePullRequest)` line (today's guessed `merge refused` gone); `bash tests/run.sh 61-needs` stays green, its lines updated where they read that stderr.

`ORIGIN_WAITS="5 15 30 60 120"` in lib/config.sh, documented in templates/user/config.sh, `HARNESS_ORIGIN_WAITS` overriding it as `HARNESS_LIMIT_SLEEP` does the limit sleep; `origin_try <m> <what> <command…>` in lib/record.sh runs the command with stderr appended to run.log, each failed try one run.log line `<m>: <what> failed (try <k> of <n>; next in <s> s)`, a success after a failure one note `<m>: <what> succeeded on try <k> (origin unreachable for <s> s)`, the last failure returning the command's exit with `ORIGIN_TRIES=<n> ORIGIN_SECS=<s>` set; a `GraphQL:` line or `(pre-receive hook declined)` on stderr ends it after one try. Three checks in 88-origin-outage.sh in a plain shell (`HARNESS_HOME=$HH`, `source lib/record.sh`, `HARNESS_ORIGIN_WAITS="0 0 0"`): a command failing twice then succeeding returns 0 with two `failed (try k of 4; next in 0 s)` lines in run.log and one `succeeded on try 3` note; one failing always returns its exit after four tries with `ORIGIN_TRIES=4`; a `GraphQL:` stderr is one try.

`merge_one` wraps in origin_try its fetch of main (`fetch of main`, replacing today's one-second second try), the branch push (`push of harness-merge/<run>-<m>`), `gh pr view`/`gh pr create` (`opening its PR`) and `gh pr merge` (`merging its PR`); `merge_milestones_`'s proposed-milestone fetch, verify's tag push (`push of tag run/<run>/<m>`) and rebase's forced tag push too. Run `od1` in 88-origin-outage.sh (origin down for three fetches at the lane's merge): harness-log.md has `M1: fetch of main succeeded on try 4 (origin unreachable for <s> s)` and `M1 merged into main`, needs/ has no `merge_failed` item, the stub-curl log no `needs you` post. Run `od6` (`STUB_GH_DOWN=2` at `pr create`): `M1: opening its PR succeeded on try 3` and merged. Refusal unchanged: a run with `STUB_REFUSE_MERGE=1` shows one `gh pr merge` line in the stub's gh.log and a `merge_refused:M1` item.

`bash -n` on lib/record.sh, lib/lane.sh, tests/stub-git-down.sh and tests/stub-gh.sh; the new check names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt (LC_ALL=C sorted); `bash tests/run.sh 88-origin` and `bash tests/run.sh 61-needs` end with every check passing before the session ends.
The suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` in the session and `bash tests/run.sh` print `N/M checks passed` with none failing.

features.description: A merge step that outlasts the retries leaves a note, a `merge_failed` needs card and a notification, harness-log.md says `verified and tagged` only when origin took the tag, a lane never closes `needs Michael` without a card, and the record and lane branches' push streaks are noted once at their start and once at their end.
steps: Run `od2` in tests/checks/88-origin-outage.sh, written first and watched failing (origin down from the verify's tag push until after the run's end, `HARNESS_ORIGIN_WAITS="0 0 0"`): harness-log.md has `M1 verified; tag run/od2/M1 is local only (push failed 4 times over <s> s; see run.log)` and no `M1 verified and tagged`; run.log has ` ! [remote rejected] run/od2/M1 -> run/od2/M1 (failure)` and `push of harness/od2 failed` lines; harness-log.md has exactly one `record branch: push of harness/od2 failed; retrying at every sync (see run.log)` and `M1: merge failed at fetch of main after 4 tries over <s> s; merged later: harness merge od2` and `lane M1 closed (M1 needs Michael: its merge (origin unreachable at fetch of main))`; needs/*.json has `merge_failed:M1` with `.card.commands == ["harness merge od2"]` and `.what == "fetch of main"`; the stub-curl log has one post with `Title: [od2] M1 needs you` and `Priority: high` and the run-end post; the state dir has `tag-local-M1` and `merge-failed-M1`.

lib/lane.sh verify tags locally as today and pushes the tag through origin_try: success keeps `<m> verified and tagged run/<run>/<m>`; failure past the retries notes the `local only` form and sets `tag-local-<m>`; `merge_one` pushes the tag first (`push of tag run/<run>/<m>`) while `tag-local-<m>` exists and clears it on success; rebase's re-tag does the same. `od2` continues: the origin-down flag removed, `harness merge od2` prints `M1 merged into main`, `git -C origin.git tag -l run/od2/M1` prints the tag, needs/done/ holds the item resolved `milestone merged`, and harness-log.md has `record branch: push of harness/od2 succeeded after <n> failures over <m> min`.

`merge_one` past the retries: `needs-<m>`, `lanes/<m>/need` = `its merge (origin unreachable at <what>)` when LDIR is set, the marker `merge-failed-<m>` holding `<what>`, the note, a needs record of the new reason `merge_failed` in lib/needs.mjs (subject `<m>`, kind needs_michael, block, high; fields what, tries, secs, tag_local, head; headline `<m>: merge failed at <what> (origin unreachable)`; why naming origin_try in lib/record.sh and the step; where run.log and the lane branch; options wait and `harness merge <run>` (recommended) or merge the PR by hand; commands `["harness merge <run>"]`), then needs_you with title `[<run>] <m> needs you`; once per `<what>` per milestone while the marker holds it, cleared on the next success past that step. Its sweep rule: `merged-<m>` → `milestone merged`; marker gone → `merge went through`; else kept. tests/fixtures/needs/merge_failed.json renders under tests/checks/59-needs-cards.sh's FILLED rule; tests/unit/needs.test.mjs's REASONS line and its fixtures count become 17 and the sweep rule's three outcomes are tested.

`lane_done` in lib/lane.sh gains two branches before its last: `refused-<m>` → `<m> needs Michael: merge refused`; the last else opens a `merge_failed` record with `what=unknown` and needs_you before `lane_exit 12 "<m> needs Michael: its merge"`. The invariant check in 88-origin-outage.sh, over every run of the file: for each `lane <m> closed (<m> needs Michael: …)` line in its harness-log.md, a needs/*.json or needs/done/*.json item of that run has `milestone == <m>` and `at` no later than the close; tests/checks/61-needs-git.sh's refused lane closes `(M2 needs Michael: merge refused)`.

`sync_record_` keeps `log "push of harness/<run> failed"` per failure and adds the streak: the first failure after a success writes `push-failing` (`<epoch> 1`) and `sync_record` notes `record branch: push of harness/<run> failed; retrying at every sync (see run.log)` outside the lock; each further failure bumps the count; the first success removes it and notes `record branch: push of harness/<run> succeeded after <n> failures over <m> min`. `sync_lane` gets the same under `lane-push-failing-<m>` with `lane <m>: push of harness-lane/<run>/<m> failed; retrying at every sync (see run.log)` and its succeeded form; `od2` asserts exactly one start note of each streak that happened.

`bash -n` on lib/record.sh, lib/lane.sh and lib/needs.sh; `node --check lib/needs.mjs`; names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `bash tests/run.sh 88-origin`, `bash tests/run.sh 61-needs`, `bash tests/run.sh 59-needs` and `bash tests/run.sh 00-unit` end with every check passing before the session ends.
The suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` in the session and `bash tests/run.sh` print `N/M checks passed` with none failing.

features.description: `harness gc` keeps a run with a verified, unmerged milestone whose tag is not on origin/main, and `harness merge <run>` works after the worktree is gone: it needs no spec, makes the worktree, restores the record from origin/main or the ledger, and fetches a missing tag.
steps: Runs `od3`, `od4` and `od5` in tests/checks/88-origin-outage.sh, written first and watched failing. `od3` (od2's state before its merge): `harness gc proj` prints `keeps <wt>: M1 verified, not merged (harness merge od3)` and leaves `harness/od3` on origin.git and the worktree, `--dry-run` and `--all-merged` print the same line, its needs items are not closed `by sweep: run removed`; then `git worktree remove --force <wt>` by hand and `harness merge od3` prints `worktree <wt> on harness/od3 (from origin/harness/od3; harness merge)` and `M1 merged into main`. `od4` (`MERGE_POLICY=pr`, `RECORD_PR=end`: M1 proposed, the record PR merged, the worktree and the origin's branch removed by hand): `harness merge od4` prints `(from origin/main; harness merge)`, no restore note, and M1 merges by its PR. `od5` (as od3 with `RECORD_PR=off` and the ledger copy deleted): `harness merge od5: no record for od5 (not on harness/od5, origin/main or <ledger>/proj/od5)`, exit 1, no worktree left; with the ledger copy present instead: `HARNESS: record restored from the ledger` committed and noted, M1 merged.

`cmd_gc` in bin/harness: a run with `verified-<m>` and no `merged-<m>` whose tag `run/<run>/<m>` is not an ancestor of origin/main after gc's fetch keeps its worktree and every branch of the run with the `keeps` line above; a milestone Michael merged by hand (the tag on origin/main) no longer holds it: a check in 88-origin-outage.sh merges od3's tag into origin.git's main by hand and sees gc remove the run.

`cmd_merge` → `cmd_start` under `HARNESS_MERGE_ONLY`: the `die` asking for `--spec`, `SPEC_FILES` or `--brief` is skipped; with no worktree one is made on `harness/<run>` from `origin/harness/<run>` when it exists, else from `origin/main`, printed `worktree <wt> on harness/<run> (from <ref>; harness merge)`; when `.harness/runs/<run>/feature_list.json` is absent the record directory is restored from origin/main's `.harness/runs/<run>/` first, else the ledger's `<ledger>/<project>/<run>/`, committed `HARNESS: record restored from <main|the ledger>` and noted; with none the `no record` line, exit 1, and the worktree it made removed again.

Each milestone's tag is the local `run/<run>/<m>`, fetched with `git fetch origin tag run/<run>/<m>` when missing locally; missing in both, `<m>: tag run/<run>/<m> is gone; not merged` and the next milestone. Checks in 88-origin-outage.sh: od4 with its local tag deleted before `harness merge od4` fetches it and merges; a run with the tag deleted locally and on origin.git prints the `is gone` line and exits 0.

`bash -n bin/harness`; the usage header of bin/harness's gc and merge commands say the keep rule and the record restore; names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `bash tests/run.sh 88-origin` and `bash tests/run.sh 08-scope` (gc's own checks) end with every check passing before the session ends.
The suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` in the session and `bash tests/run.sh` print `N/M checks passed` with none failing.

features.description: With `HOURS` empty or 0 a run has no end time: `DEADLINE=0`, every reader of it treats 0 as none, `limit_wait` still waits for a usage-limit window, the clock line and run.log's first line say `no end time`, and `--until` or a whole-number `HOURS` still end a run.
steps: A new tests/checks/89-no-deadline.sh (its tier on line 2 by journal/decisions/2026-11-03-suite-tiers.md's 30 s rule, timed once with `TEST_JOBS=4 bash tests/run.sh 89-no-deadline`; its names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and, when fast, check-names-fast.txt), written first and watched failing: a stub run `nd` with `HOURS=` in its run.env and no `--until`: run.log's first line ends `· no end time`, the coding prompt's line matches `Clock: … · run [0-9]+h[0-9]{2}m \(no end time\) · this session: …`, `ended` starts `done`, no `deadline reached` note; a run `nd2` with `HOURS=` whose shared limit file (`LIMIT_FILE`, `<state root>/LIMIT_UNTIL`) is planted 3 s ahead before its first coding session: `usage-limit window (shared by all runs): waiting until <HH:MM> (0 min)` is noted before `session 1` in run.log (today's code skips the wait once `DEADLINE=0`); `resolve_ok` sourced in a plain shell with `DEADLINE=0` is not refused for the deadline; `HOURS=1` in run.env gives `· ends <HH:MM>` and the clock's `of 1h, ends` form.

lib/driver.sh: `DEADLINE=0` when `HOURS` is empty or 0; `T0 + HOURS * 3600` for a whole number over 0; `DEADLINE_AT` set gives it, or the earlier of the two; run.log's first line gains `· ends <HH:MM>` or `· no end time`; `HARNESS_DEADLINE=0` reaches the lanes.

Every reader treats 0 as none: lib/driver.sh's two deadline tests in the poll loop, lib/lane.sh's three reads in the lane loop, `limit_wait` in lib/record.sh caps the wait at the deadline only when there is one, lib/resolve.sh's `less than RESOLVE_TIMEOUT before the deadline` only with a deadline, `deadline_verify` unreached without one; `clock()` keeps `run 3h10m of 8h, ends 03:55` with a deadline and prints `run 3h10m (no end time)` without; the check `the prompt says the time, the budget and the attempt` in tests/checks/08-scope-sh-l1-02-run-capped-services-gc-scratch.sh, 13-run-2-michael-sets-desk.sh, 14-run-2b-stop-records.sh and 15-run-4-same-but-queue-parked-debrief-tmux.sh accepts both forms.

features.description: The pure rules of a fix round exist and are unit-tested before any wiring: `fix-add` in lib/features.mjs builds the fix feature, `fix-round` in lib/metrics.mjs writes the `fix_round` and `fix_result` rows, lib/summary.mjs counts them into `fix_rounds` and a `Fix rounds` report row, `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS=2` is configured, and the stub suite and stub claude of tests/checks/90-fix-rounds.sh carry the markers the runs need.
steps: tests/unit/features.test.mjs, written first and watched failing: `fixFeature` yields `{ id: "<m>-fix<r>", milestone, kind: "fix", issue: "all", round, after: [<the milestone's last feature id in list order>], model: <WORKER_MODEL>, fix_names, fix_files, fix_out, description, steps, passes: false }` with the description `fix round <r> of <m>: the full suite is red on the verified tree (<k> failing: <up to 5 names>[ +n])` (` +n` only past five names) and the three steps of the spec's item 2 (`<check> <files>` exits 0 naming the out file, `<check> --fast` exits 0, `<check>` exits 0); `lint` prints nothing for it; `kindOf` returns `fix`; `repairList` with the appended feature in `before` keeps it; the CLI `fix-add <list> <m> <r> <issue> <names…> -- <files…> -- <out> <check>` appends it to the list file and prints the id.

tests/unit/metrics.test.mjs: `fixRound` gives `{ kind: "fix_round", run, milestone, round, issue, feature, failed_before, files_before, at }` and `fixResult` gives `{ kind: "fix_result", run, milestone, round, issue, failed_after, fixed, at }` with `fixed` true exactly when `failed_after` is empty; the CLI `fix-round` appends one such row to a metrics.jsonl path.

tests/unit/summary.test.mjs: `fixRounds(rows)` returns `{ opened, fixed, by_milestone: { "<m>": { opened, fixed } } }` pairing each `fix_result` to its `fix_round` by milestone and round; `build` adds `fix_rounds`; the report row `Fix rounds` comes after `Flakes` with the texts `2 opened · 1 fixed (M1 1 of 1, M2 0 of 1)` and `0`, no row for a summary without the key; `Spend by role` lists `fix`.
`MAX_FIX_ROUNDS=2` in lib/config.sh and documented in templates/user/config.sh.

A new tests/checks/90-fix-rounds.sh (`# tier: slow` on line 2) with tests/checks/87-fast-gate-run.sh's two-tier stub suite extended: bare red on `BROKEN`, `BROKEN-SLOW` (`FAIL t1 (BROKEN-SLOW)`, `HARNESS_FAILED=t1`) or `BROKEN-SLOW2` (`FAIL t3 (BROKEN-SLOW2)`, `HARNESS_FAILED=t3`); `--tier fast` red on `BROKEN` or `BROKEN-FAST`; a subset red only on the named file's marker (`t1` on `BROKEN-SLOW`, `t3` on `BROKEN-SLOW2`); `STUB_FLAKE_ONCE=1` makes the first bare call after `flake-armed` exists red (`FAIL t2`, `HARNESS_FAILED=t2`) and removes it; four checks in a plain shell prove those four forms. tests/stub-claude.sh's coding branch for an id matching `*-fix[0-9]*`: `STUB_FIX=rename` moves `BROKEN-SLOW` to `BROKEN-SLOW2`, `STUB_FIX=fix` removes both, `STUB_FIX=none` leaves them, and the second fix session of a run is always `none`; its usage header documents them.

`node --check` on lib/features.mjs, lib/metrics.mjs and lib/summary.mjs; `bash -n` on tests/stub-claude.sh and lib/config.sh; the unit names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt, 90's in check-names.txt; `node --test --test-isolation=none tests/unit/*.test.mjs` and `bash tests/run.sh 90-fix` end with every test passing before the session ends.
The suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` in the session and `bash tests/run.sh` print `N/M checks passed` with none failing.

features.description: A verify whose full suite is red opens a fix round instead of a card while `fix-rounds-<m>` is under `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS`: the fix feature is appended, the lane's next session fixes it under a `{{FIX}}` prompt line and a `green_fix` gate, and the verify runs again and tags `(after fix round <r>)`.
steps: Run `fx1` in tests/checks/90-fix-rounds.sh (`STUB_SLOW_RED=B STUB_FIX=fix`), written first and watched failing: B passes on the fast tier; harness-log.md has `verify M1: the suite is red on the verified tree (main had nothing new: a slow-tier red the fast gate let through); fix round 1 of 2: M1-fix1 appended (1 failing: t1)` and no `needs Michael`; no `needs-M1` in the state dir, no `verify_red` item in needs/, no `needs you` post in the stub-curl log; `jq` on the record's feature_list.json shows `M1-fix1` with `kind` `fix`, `issue` `all`, `round` 1, `after` `["B"]`, `fix_names` `["t1"]`, `fix_files` `["t1"]` and three steps, and `node lib/features.mjs lint` prints nothing for the list; `.harness/runs/fx1/fix/M1-1.out` is in the record with the `FAIL t1` line; the fix session's prompt has `Fix round 1 of 2` naming `t1` and the out path; suite-args.log shows `t1` then `--tier fast` after the fix session's line; run.log has `M1-fix1 · … · passes=true`; two `verify M1` sessions; `M1 verified and tagged run/fx1/M1 (after fix round 1)` and merged; metrics.jsonl has a `fix_round` row (`failed_before ["t1"]`), a `fix_result` row (`failed_after []`, `fixed true`) and the fix session's row with `role fix`; summary.json has `fix_rounds.opened 1` and `fixed 1`; `harness report fx1 --md` prints `Fix rounds | 1 opened · 1 fixed (M1 1 of 1)`; `verify-rounds-M1` is 1.

lib/lane.sh verify: `result=red` with `fix-rounds-<m>` under `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` opens round `r = fix-rounds-<m> + 1` (written; `verify-rounds-<m>` put back to its value before this verify): the names from the lane's check-<key>.out (`red-<key>`'s stored names when the marker exists, else the output's last `HARNESS_FAILED=` line and every `FAIL <name>` line; no `HARNESS_FAILED=` line gives the files `whole suite`), its last 200 lines copied to `.harness/runs/<run>/fix/<m>-<r>.out` and committed, `F fix-add` under the record lock with `repair`'s before.json snapshotted after the append, the `fix_round` row through `MET fix-round`, the note above, no `needs-<m>`, record or notification; `verify` returns 1 and the lane loop's next pick is the fix feature.

The fix session: a `{{FIX}}` slot in prompts/coding.md and lib/prompt.sh, rendered empty for every other feature (as `{{REVIEW_DIFF}}`), under *This session* for a `kind fix` feature as `Fix round <r> of <max>: the full suite is red on this milestone's verified tree; failing: <names>; its output: <fix_out>; your feature passes on \`<check> <files>\` and \`<check> --fast\` green, and the verify then runs the full suite.`; prompts/coding.md gets a paragraph for `kind: fix` (fix the cause, never a check's assertion; a check that was wrong is changed with its reason in the entry); after the session, for `kind == fix`, `green_fix` in lib/record.sh runs `"$CHECK" <fix_files>` (the full suite when the files are `whole suite`) and `green_fast`, a red un-passing it with the note `<id> un-passed: <check <files>|fast tier> red after the session`; its metrics row's `role` is `fix`.

The verify again: the fix passing makes the milestone done, the next verify re-runs every step and the full suite, and hold-and-green notes `<m> verified and tagged run/<run>/<m> (after fix round <r>)` before the tag and merge, with the `fix_result` row written at that suite verdict. Run `fx5` in 90-fix-rounds.sh (`STUB_SLOW_RED=B STUB_FIX=none`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS=1` in run.env): harness-log.md has `M1-fix1 un-passed: check t1 red after the session`, needs/ has a `given_up` item for `M1-fix1`, and `ended` reads `blocked on M1-fix1`.

`bash -n` on lib/lane.sh, lib/record.sh and lib/prompt.sh; names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `bash tests/run.sh 90-fix` and `bash tests/run.sh 87-fast-gate` end with every check passing before the session ends.
The suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` in the session and `bash tests/run.sh` print `N/M checks passed` with none failing.

features.description: The rounds are bounded and counted: at `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` the verify opens today's `verify_red` card naming every round and what each left standing, `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS=0` is today's behaviour from the first red, a flake never opens a round, and every round's `fix_result` row pairs with its `fix_round`.
steps: Runs `fx2`, `fx3` and `fx4` in tests/checks/90-fix-rounds.sh, written first and watched failing. `fx2` (`STUB_SLOW_RED=B STUB_FIX=rename`): round 1 on `t1`, the fix session passes its gate, the second verify is red on `t3` and notes `fix round 2 of 2: M1-fix2 appended (1 failing: t3)`, its session renames nothing more and passes its gate, the third verify is red and notes `verify M1: the suite is red on the verified tree (main had nothing new: a slow-tier red the fast gate let through); not verified (needs Michael) after 2 fix rounds (M1-fix1, M1-fix2)`; `needs-M1` exists, the `verify_red:M1` item has `variant own` and a `why` naming both rounds and each round's `failed_after`; one `[fx2] M1 needs you` post; `ended` reads `waiting on Michael` as today; metrics.jsonl rows: round 1 `failed_before ["t1"]`, `failed_after ["t3"]`, `fixed false`; round 2 `["t3"]`, `["t3"]`, `false`; summary.json `fix_rounds.opened 2, fixed 0`; `harness report fx2 --md` prints `2 opened · 0 fixed (M1 0 of 2)`. `fx3` (`STUB_FLAKE_ONCE=1`, `flake-armed` planted before the verify): `flaky: t2` noted, `M1 verified and tagged run/fx3/M1`, no `fix` feature in the list, `fix_rounds.opened 0`, the report row `0`. `fx4` (`MAX_FIX_ROUNDS=0` in run.env, `STUB_SLOW_RED=B`): today's `verify_red` card at the first red, no feature appended, no `fix_round` row.

lib/lane.sh verify at `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS`: today's red path with the note's `after <n> fix rounds (<ids>)` suffix, the `fix_result` row for the last round written before the card, the `verify_red` card's `why` gaining the rounds, their ids and each `fix_result`'s `failed_after` (lib/needs.mjs reads them from the fields the shell passes), its notification as today; `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS=0` never opens a round; the rule fires only on `result=red` after the rerun guard, so a `flaky:` note and a fix feature never both come from one verify.

tests/unit/needs.test.mjs: the `verify_red` card from tests/fixtures/needs/verify_red.json with a `rounds` field renders its `why` naming each round's id and names and stays FILLED under tests/checks/59-needs-cards.sh's rule; without the field the card reads as today.

`bash -n lib/lane.sh`; `node --check lib/needs.mjs`; names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt (the unit names); `bash tests/run.sh 90-fix`, `bash tests/run.sh 59-needs` and `bash tests/run.sh 00-unit` end with every check passing before the session ends.
The suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` in the session and `bash tests/run.sh` print `N/M checks passed` with none failing.

features.description: Review + simplify of M3: an Opus reviewer reads the milestone diff from a file (hardest: the rule firing only on `result=red` after the rerun guard, `verify-rounds-<m>` put back, the fix feature surviving `repair` and `lane_guard`, `green_fix`'s two gates, the rows' pairing by milestone and round, the card naming every round), Critical/Important findings fixed RED→GREEN, the decision file journal/decisions/2026-11-04-fix-rounds.md written, docs/architecture.md, README.md and templates/user/config.sh updated.
steps: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib bin tests templates prompts > /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-11-04-2/M3-diff.patch` (the run directory left out); an Opus subagent reviews that file with the spec's M3 section and its hardest list as the brief, reading every fix-session change in tests/checks/90-fix-rounds.sh's runs for an assertion edited to pass; one round by default and a second only when the first found something Critical; the findings go in the entry's summary as `<n> Critical, <n> Important, <n> Minor`.

Every Critical or Important finding gets a check in tests/checks/90-fix-rounds.sh or the unit files that is red before its fix and green after (the pairs listed in the entry's `verified_how`); Minor ones are fixed or listed as left.

A simplification pass on lib/lane.sh's verify (one red branch deciding round or card; the names read once) and lib/summary.mjs's pairing applied where `bash tests/run.sh 90-fix` and `bash tests/run.sh 00-unit` stay green; `bash -n` and `node --check` on every file touched.

journal/decisions/2026-11-04-fix-rounds.md: title, provenance, finding (the red verify's card today and the fast gate's slow-tier reds), choice (items 1–4 of the spec's M3 with every default marked *default*: `fix-rounds-<m>` kept across continues, `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS=2`, `issue: all`, the two rows, the counters), rejected (the verifier deciding to loop; un-passing the milestone's features; fixing in the verify session; unlimited rounds; a triage session now, F2's trigger named).

docs/architecture.md §5 (the verify step: red → fix round → verify again), §6 (the feature-list contract: `kind fix`, `issue`, `round`, `fix_names`, `fix_files`, `fix_out`; the driver as the one list writer besides the initializer and repair), §4 (`fix-rounds-<m>`, `<run dir>/fix/`), §7 (a `Fix round` row), §10 (`MAX_FIX_ROUNDS`), §11 (the `Fix rounds` measure); README.md *What a run is* (a red verify opens a fix round) and the report's rows (`Fix rounds`); templates/user/config.sh's `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` line consistent with both.
The suite is green: `bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` in the session and `bash tests/run.sh` print `N/M checks passed` with none failing.
